title: A complex is pseudo-coherent exactly when it is m-pseudo-coherent for all m, and then its finite free resolution can be chosen to vanish above the top cohomology

standard_prerequisites.name: Bounded complexes of finite free or finite projective R-modules and the stupid truncation sigma_{>= m} of a complex

standard_prerequisites.name: The cone of a morphism of complexes of R-modules together with the long exact cohomology sequence of the resulting distinguished triangle
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 16102-16112, where the cone is the one of Derived Categories, Definition derived-definition-cone
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the two prescribed cohomological properties of the partially built map alpha into the vanishing of H^i(C^bullet) for i >= n, which is what lets the induction step be restarted one degree lower.

core_obligations: Handle the easy direction (1) => (3), which only uses that a finite free module is a finite projective module, and then prove (3) => (1) by manufacturing a bounded above complex F^bullet of finite free modules out of a bounded above complex P^bullet of finite projective modules: choose a direct sum decomposition F^{n_0} = P^{n_0} + C^{n_0} in the top degree and then inductively F^{n - 1} = P^{n - 1} + C^n + C^{n - 1}, with differentials that agree with P^{n - 1} -> P^n, induce the identity C^n -> C^n and vanish on C^{n - 1} (proof lines 16063-16076).

Observe that the comparison map F^bullet -> P^bullet built that way is a homotopy equivalence, hence a quasi-isomorphism, so that (3) does imply pseudo-coherence without any appeal to finiteness of cohomology (proof lines 16075-16076).

Prove (1) => (2) by taking a bounded above complex E^bullet of finite free modules quasi-isomorphic to K^bullet and exhibiting, for each integer m, the map sigma_{>= m}E^bullet -> K^bullet from the stupid truncation, which is a bounded complex of finite free modules whose comparison map is an isomorphism in degrees > m and surjective in degree m (proof lines 16079-16084).

Prove (2) => (3) together with the refinement by descending induction on n: construct finite free R-modules F^i for i >= n, differentials d^i : F^i -> F^{i + 1} and compatible maps alpha : F^i -> K^i such that H^i(alpha) is an isomorphism for i > n and surjective for i = n while F^i = 0 for i > b, starting from the base case n = b + 1 (proof lines 16086-16101).

Carry out the induction step: form the cone C^bullet on the partially constructed alpha, read off H^i(C^bullet) = 0 for i >= n from the long exact cohomology sequence, apply lemma-cone-pseudo-coherent and lemma-finite-cohomology to see that the kernel of H^n(F^bullet) -> H^n(K^bullet) is a finite R-module, hit it by a finite free module F^{n - 1}, extend the diagram of complexes, and finally correct F^{n - 1} to F^{n - 1} + R^{oplus r} so that the cokernel of H^{n - 1}(F^bullet) -> H^{n - 1}(K^bullet) is killed by the new free summand (proof lines 16102-16141).
proof_roadmap: (1) => (3) is immediate; for (3) => (1) build a bounded above complex of finite free modules F^bullet together with a homotopy equivalence F^bullet -> P^bullet by the telescoping decompositions F^{n_0} = P^{n_0} + C^{n_0} and F^{n - 1} = P^{n - 1} + C^n + C^{n - 1} (proof lines 16063-16076).
(1) => (2): truncate a bounded above finite free resolution E^bullet -> K^bullet with sigma_{>= m} to obtain the witness of m-pseudo-coherence for each m (proof lines 16079-16084).

(2) => (3): run a descending induction on n in which a finite free module F^{n - 1} is adjoined so that the cohomology map becomes an isomorphism in degree n - 1 and stays surjective in degree n, the induction being driven by the cone on alpha and the two cited finiteness lemmas (proof lines 16086-16141).
The same induction carries the vanishing bound F^i = 0 for i > b along, which yields the final sentence of the statement (proof lines 16094-16101 and 16141).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes pseudo-coherence of a complex K over an arbitrary ring in three equivalent ways and appends a vanishing refinement: if the cohomology of K vanishes above b, then the quasi-isomorphism from a bounded above complex of finite free modules to K can be chosen with the same vanishing bound (statement lines 16049-16059). The direction (3) => (1) is not a citation but a construction: a bounded above complex of finite projective modules is rebuilt as one of finite free modules by the telescoping direct sum decompositions in the top degree and one degree lower, arranged so that the comparison map is even a homotopy equivalence (proof lines 16064-16076). The substantial part is (2) => (3) together with the vanishing bound, a descending induction on n in which finite free modules, their differentials and compatible maps to K are built so that the comparison map on cohomology is an isomorphism above n and surjective in degree n; the induction step passes through the cone on the partially built map, the long exact cohomology sequence, and the two cited lemmas lemma-cone-pseudo-coherent and lemma-finite-cohomology, and then needs a final correction of the module in degree n - 1 by a free summand in order to kill the cokernel there (proof lines 16086-16141). The bookkeeping of two cohomological properties plus a vanishing range at once, with the correction step at the end, is what keeps this out of the routine range; no step of the argument is replaced by a citation.
